eras.summary: Sandpoint burning: Durdun Pallwick lost shop and stock (48 gold left); Ammut funded 102 gold silent partnership. Daeris: 40 years bound to debt ledger, outlasted three contract holders. Three bodies found with Thassilonian greed runes carved into chests. Scarred Man's entity possessed Hemlock; Morwen exorcised it via chalk wards. Hemlock named school: Greed, linked to Karzoug soul-harvest. Junction stone beneath Sandpoint cathedral destroyed, cutting Thistletop's harvest feed. Hemwick (expelled scholar, 11 days underground) confirmed larger 10,000-year harvest reservoir beneath Thistletop headland. Decoy disc floated upstream; three spawn attacked empty cottage. Chasm spawn rider killed by Ammut (shadow blade, 31 damage); Ammut took 14 damage, broken ribs. Shalelu confirmed spawn moving south in formation. Blasting powder (4 charges) purchased from Corven Coldwater; missing brother Aldus Vareth entered sea cave 7 years ago, never returned

Thistletop undercroft: charmed broken goblin warned of wrongness in left passage; took right, neutralized three guards, opened Thassilonian iron door with recovered keys. Descended into ancient blue-lit chamber. Found Nualia and robed man Hemwick-associate copying channel script. Silence spell deployed; Nualia wounded but survived first strike, Morwen cut off her invocation, shadow blade through crown killed her without final words. Robed man captured, named facility a ten-thousand-year greed reservoir near activation. Daeris revealed as Collector informant forty years, debt-ledger entry at age seventeen, eye-shift confirmed. Party chose to keep her.

Blew junction stone; Thassilonian caretaker-creature stood aside. Found Aldus Vareth alive at sea-cave terminus. Returned Aldus to Sandpoint; Father Zantus confirmed he'd live. Reservoir not destroyed—still feeding, pressure-releasing through goblin skin-cuts after stone channels severed. Collector identified in Varisia personally, walking among goblins toward Whisperwood marker stone.

Party rode to Whisper

Sandpoint, Foxglove Manor arc: Ammut, Daeris, Morwen, Frizwick became a four-person unit. Skinsaw murders investigated; frost-rune corpses found, souls harvested on Thassilonian altar feeding entity Karzoug before solstice. Foxglove Manor: 43 sketches of Ammut, sealed altar, three animated bodies, northeast coastal anchor point still active. Foxglove subdued, extracted. Cipher wheel cracked soul-harvest ledger. The Seventh (unnamed woman) ran Sandpoint circuit; Ammut killed her, seized iron box, brass token, records. Tharwick (local operative) identified; replacement Third was Aldus Vareth. Vareth rescued from Salter's Row before harbour ship departed. Harvest schedule accelerating; Spire destination confirmed; senior structure above Seventh unknown.

Three unnamed workers killed at Fogscar shaft during arch demolition. All four Thassilonian soul-collection sites destroyed: northeast sea cave anchor (blasting charges), Fogscar processing facility (three charges, arch rubble). Amber vials recovered from Zantus's cabinet and cliff cache. Rinn Toldrath killed, body in harbour. Tharwick broken, cipher drop made buying 5-6 days. Vareth alive, moved to temple. Scarred Woman (Marta/Pellwick Imports courier) overdue, circuit dark. Upper contact uses Cooper Street dead drop. Edric Solm named. Solstice: 11 days. Network has no working collection infrastructure.

Shaft dig: two inscription workers killed by rigged blast, intent-check stripped from sorter. Third survivor escaped via pre-cut crawlspace. Pursued to ridge; captured Karvun Emberveil (Eastern operative, jaw scar). Fey charm extracted name: Edric, closed-eye cipher. Ammut killed Karvun on the scree. Rode south to Charred Barrel inn. Followed contact Korunn through hidden tunnel to underground chamber. Ammut killed Edric (robed, faceless); took hand, knee, head. Looted: pouch, ring, papers, pendant, vellum scrap with four words, cipher letters, drop points. Korunn flipped; confirmed seven seats above Edric, Third seat vacant, solstice deadline. Network mapped but top leadership unknown and faceless. Hemlock briefed; reported missing couples, unmarked skiff, threatening flowers. Catacombs investigation: gate recently oiled, fresh footprints, soft candle wax. Two robed figures performing binding ritual at altar bearing carved closed eye. Killed both plus a partially transformed entity. Recovered unrecogn

Sandpoint cult operation concluded. Party destroyed Thassilonian altar (10,000-year-old bloodfeeding channel) via explosives under Sandpoint and a sea cave north of town. Edric dead; tallow-skinned construct destroyed; three cave cultists killed; two rowers unaccounted for. Recovered brass tokens predate Edric's system—liturgical, not administrative. Pale Choir identified as name for what the ritual feeds, not the congregation. Vessa (ex-acolyte) extracted and sheltered. North-quarter couple murdered by Choir contact; scarred woman spotted beforehand. Buried entity beneath cliff partially collapsed; threat unresolved. Shalelu reported Thistletop power vacuum post-Nualia. Daeris proposed to and accepted; now fourth wife. Korunn withheld one name; suspected to be the Third.

Korunn charmed and revealed: formerly the Third under a woman called Aunt, who bears a burned spiral scar on her collarbone matching the sea cave door. Aunt predates Edric's network and references debts owed to something old. The sea cave is a blood-keyed entrance, not smuggling infrastructure. Inside: a shrine with scheduled bone deposits, a conduit-body with metal ribs (rune broken post-death), a blood-groove feeding the cave, a black pool creature carrying a spiral disc, and a gold-inlaid throne room below. Eight alcoves held a preserved former Third; burning her cracked the stone and silenced the floor. Traffickers found in a connected hand-dug tunnel discussed the Spire and Aunt casually. All were killed. A count-keeper revealed Aunt runs everything and the Spire is something she serves or channels. A strongbox held a docility vial and a letter on Tharwick's paper. Two captives freed; a third, Yassa, dead past a barred door guarded by a creature. Daeris questioned Yassa's corpse: Aunt is a vessel for something else;

Ambushed/killed slavers on Sandpoint road; captured wagons holding chained prisoners. Informant named Aunt — a face-changer running the operation personally. Caster Dunmoor surrendered; freed four captives with Hemlock's aid. Entered Fogscar tunnels; found Shalelu investigating claw-kill corpses (no blade, no feeding — something built, not born). Destroyed a flesh-workshop and two stitched constructs via charges; collapsed tunnel. Encountered second larger entity — fled, barely. Frizwick wounded. Two creatures, thousand miles apart, marked by identical ancient spirals predating Karzoug. Hemlock notified; Magnimar alerted. Returned to Sandpoint. Thistletop now mustering under unknown cloaked commander (not alive) with disciplined goblin force and purpose-made siege ladders. Morwen/Daeris ride for Hemlock. Ammut/Frizwick/Shalelu rig gully with six charges. Column approaching.

Sandpoint region secured. Fogscar workshop destroyed: six unfinished constructs, one active Sleeper killed after hand regrowth, burned post-mortem. Spiral discs recovered — Thassilonian origin, ten thousand years old. Yassa found dead in sea cave; Speak with Dead revealed "Aunt," a northern trade network using goblin trail markers, ledger evidence. Goblin muster broken at gully ambush. Party travels to Magnimar. Fish Alley contact Chask Haladan spooked by name "Edric"; rival scarred investigator asking same questions, directed uptown toward "Marasova." Party undetected, secured lodging, Alabaster District next.

Magnimar, Fish Alley / Alabaster District. Party (Ammut, Frizwick, Morwen, Daeris) identified child-trafficking operation run through Chask Haladan's warehouse. Chask interrogated: named child "Sable," confirmed female operative called the Collector (also posing as "Marasova") and destination "the Spire." Ammut killed Chask; warehouse burned with ledger and evidence. Spire scouted: kill-ward discharged via crossbow bolt. Interior cleared — two Drowned Graftings killed, robed corpse found bearing brass token. Grafter Ilvane Threcker (rank Seven) captured alive. Confirmed: numbered rank structure, iron rings are one-way tracking devices, rank Four presumed dead at Fogscar. "Sable" is a name attached to a failed delivery, not a person met directly. Network extends upward — "the mountain," consistent with giant activity near Jorgenfist in the Kodars. Rumored rank One unconfirmed. Spire cleared.

Sandpoint arc: Party (Ammut, Frizwick, Daeris, Morwen) investigates trafficking workshop. Ilvane used as bait, captures Durnah; both confirmed as grafted test subjects of same unknown handler. Ilvane killed at her request. Durnah interrogated, names Sable (child-sized Collector courier, 2-day check-in window), then killed. Workshop and intake room burned. Second ledger's header script predates the trafficking network—system was inherited, not invented. Sable ambush intercepted empty cart: note confirming group was expected, newer ledger showing workshop retired deliberately, child's glove left as message. Jorgenfist (mountain staging ground) no longer needs the Spire. Free horse acquired. Shalelu contacted for map, meeting pending. Wyla Ashvane (canal-district enchanter) commissioned: four cold-iron anti-magic rings, blood-bound, 1200gp, 5-day timeline. Mokmurian identified as Thassilonian-caliber wizard threat.

answers.q: What did the party learn about Korunn Quellvane's past when they charmed her with her consent?
answers.expect: she had been 'the Third' before Edric, walking victims out of houses; recruited by a woman calling herself Aunt; burned spiral on her collarbone matching the sea cave door (~t1056)
answers.armA_eras:
Based on the campaign summaries, when Korunn was charmed and questioned, the party learned that she had **formerly served as the Third** in the network, operating under a woman called **"Aunt."** Aunt bears a **burned spiral scar on her collarbone** that matches the marking on the sea cave door.

The party also learned that Aunt **predates Edric's network** and references **debts owed to something old**.

It should be noted that Korunn had previously withheld one name when debriefed without charm (suspected to be the Third — which was herself), and the charming session is what revealed her former role and the details about Aunt.

However, the summaries do not describe Korunn's charm as occurring **"with her consent"** — that specific detail is not confirmed in the provided context.

answers.armA_eras:
Based on the campaign summaries provided, the context mentions a "Sleeper" being killed at the Fogscar workshop after exhibiting hand regrowth, and that it was "burned post-mortem" in the [t1299–t1410] era summary. However, the summaries do not describe any questioning of the Sleeper by Daeris or any information it revealed under questioning.

CANNOT ANSWER
answers.armB_retrieval:
Based on [T1159], the corpse revealed several things under Daeris's questioning:

1. **"Aunt" is not truly a woman** — she is described as "a coat something else wears"
2. **The Spire is a throat** — old and patient, feeding on sin and debt, specifically Karzoug's throat
3. **Its location** — north and high, past goblin roads, past dead kings cut into stone
4. **How captives are transported** — by wagon first, then handed to something that "doesn't walk like a man" for the last mile
5. **The fate of captives** — nobody carried there comes back whole

After the questioning, **the party searched the body**, finding nothing on it — no mark, no token — noting that whoever ran the operation stripped its people clean before they were used up. Then they moved on, passing the dead accountant and the count-keeper's crumpled shape, and dragged the two captives up toward the tide.

answers.q: Who did the Seventh's network intend as the replacement Third, and how did the party learn it?
answers.expect: Aldus Vareth (the man Ammut pulled out of Thistletop); Ammut overheard Tharwick and an unhurried woman in a cold-house storeroom, five minutes on the clock (~t587)
answers.armA_eras:
Based on the campaign summaries, the replacement Third was **Aldus Vareth**.

The party learned this through cracking the **cipher wheel** to read the soul-harvest ledger recovered during the Foxglove Manor arc. The summary for [t469–t627] states that after the cipher wheel cracked the soul-harvest ledger, "replacement Third was Aldus Vareth" — and notably, the party then acted on this intelligence by rescuing Vareth from Salter's Row before a harbour ship could depart with him.
answers.armB_retrieval:
Based on the retrieved context, the Seventh's network intended **Aldus Vareth** — the man Ammut had previously pulled out of Thistletop — as the replacement Third.

The party learned this through two converging sources:

1. **The cracked cipher pages** (using the cipher wheel, with the key built into the tooth-depth sequence): The decoded oilskin pages revealed a soul harvest on a schedule, with a replacement Third already identified as being of "Sandpoint provenance" (T581).

2. **Ammut's direct surveillance of Tharwick**: Ammut went alone into the cold house on the good side of the square, found Tharwick in a storeroom speaking with an unhurried, precise woman. Ammut overheard the conversation — which confirmed the northeast point was exposed, the schedule was accelerating, and named **Aldus Vareth** specifically as the intended replacement Third, with confirmation expected that night (T587).

answers.q: How did Chask Haladan die, and what did his confession give the party?
answers.expect: a fast death from Ammut's blade, then fed to a warehouse fire in Fish Alley; the confession gave Sable's name, the Collector's shape, and the Spire's existence (~t1428)
answers.armA_eras:
Based on the campaign summaries, specifically the [t1413–t1487] era:

**How he died:** Ammut killed Chask Haladan directly after his interrogation.

**What his confession gave the party:** Chask named the child **"Sable,"** confirmed a female operative called **the Collector** (also operating under the alias **"Marasova"**), and confirmed the destination of the trafficking operation as **"the Spire."** This intelligence directed the party toward the Spire, which they subsequently scouted and cleared.
answers.armB_retrieval:
Based on the retrieved chapters, Chask Haladan was killed by Ammut with a blade — described as receiving "the fast kind" of mercy before his body was consumed in the warehouse fire that Ammut set to destroy the evidence within.

His confession yielded three key pieces of intelligence:

1. **Sable** — the name of a child he claimed he never personally harmed but had "logged," meaning recorded or catalogued in the trafficking operation.
2. **The Collector** — revealed to be a scarred, smileless woman who runs collections, previously known to the party only as a rival investigator asking after Marasova, now exposed as the hand directing operations beneath the warehouse.
3. **The Spire** — a location uptown, past the Alabaster District, representing the uppermost layer of the organization above even the Collector, though Chask claimed he could not name any specific person associated with it.
